title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 396
text:
54. Judges dealing with family cases will need to delicately balance respect for different
approaches to parenting within a diverse range of cultural norms and, at the same time, aim
to protect all children from potential parental maltreatment.
414

55. Relatively newly arrived parents may originate from countries with a corrupt state apparatus
or no welfare or legal system, or where the state has no involvement in defining adequate
parenting. This can affect how parents respond to agencies, including their own solicitors.

56. In order to make a fair assessment, it is important for the court and any assessor, or other
expert, to understand cultural issues where these have affected a parent’s attitude or
behaviour.
Communicating interculturally

57. This section is about witnesses attending a hearing conducted in English, but who do not
themselves speak English as a first/native language. For a discussion of the specific rights
and needs of Welsh-speakers, see “The right to speak Welsh” below.
